html:
Barthélemy Boganda was a Catholic priest and politician who led Ubangi-Shari to self-rule and is the founding father of the Central African Republic.

Born in the Lobaye forest, he was taken in by missionaries and became the first priest from the colony. In 1946 he was elected to the French National Assembly, where he denounced forced labour. His party drew mass support across Ubangi-Shari.

He proclaimed the Central African Republic on 1 December 1958, designed its flag and wrote its anthem, hoping it would be the core of a union of the former French Equatorial Africa. He died in a plane crash in March 1959, before independence, and his death left a gap filled by weaker men such as Bokassa.
sum: Barthélemy Boganda was a Catholic priest and politician who led Ubangi-Shari to self-rule and is the founding father of the Central African Republic.
